To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentrations of aryl hydrocarbons (Ah) receptor in diploid and tetraploid cells from DEN/AAF treated rats are similar, but the levels of the 2S protein, the so-called 2S polycyclic hydrocarbon binding protein are higher in diploid cells.

1) the level of the Ah receptor is not different in diploid and tetraploid liver cells from DEN/AAF treated rats; 2) the level of 4S PAHC binding protein is twice as high in diploid as in tetraploidy liver cells from the same treatment protocol.
the concentrations of the Ah receptor and of 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) binding protein in carcinogen-induced diploids and tetraploids differ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the growth control of diploid and polylploid hepatocytes is associated with differences in the levels of aryl hydrocarbons receptor and of a 4S PAHC binding protein.

the question of whether there is a difference in the level of the aryl hydro carbon receptor and of 45 PAH binding protein between diploid and polypioid hepatocytes of 1-acetylaminoflurene (AAF)-treated rats.
the role of the Ah receptor and the 4S polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbon binding protein in the growth of diploid and polylpid hepatocytes from DEN and AAF-treated rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ah receptor is involved in the process of liver carcinogenesis, but that its role is not yet understood.
the Ah-receptor is not a major factor for hepatocarcinogenicity in the DEN/AAF model.
the Ah receptor is not the target of AAF in the process of carcinogen-induced hepatocellular hyperplasia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

diploid hepatocytes from carcinogen-exposed rats show increased growth rates and higher 4S PA-binding protein concentrations, whereas the Ah receptor concentrations are similar to those in polyploid hepatocyte populations of the same rats.
the Ah receptor does not play a role in the growth of the diploidy hepatocytes.

the Ah receptor and the 4S polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbon-binding protein are not the key determinants of the differences in growth regulation in diploid and carcinogen-treated polyploid hepatocyte populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ah receptor and the 4S polyploid hydrocarbon binding protein are present in diploid hepatocyte from DEN/AAF rats and that the concentration of the latter is significantly higher than in tetraploid cells.

the 4S polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbon (PNAH)-binding protein is present at a much higher level in diploid hepatocyte than in polyploid hepatocyte populations of rats treated with diethylenitrosamine (DENA) and 2-aceylaminofluore (AAF).

diploid hepatocytes from rats that received the carcinogens diethylnnitrosamine and 2-acetaminofluorena have twice the levels of the 45 kDa protein that binds polycyclic aromatic compounds as compared to tetraploid hepatocyte from the same rats.
